[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/02/28 (Tue) 17:16  
[USER] User inquired about the American Film Institute's criteria for eligibility for its "AFI 100 Years…" lists.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The American Film Institute determines eligibility for its "AFI 100 Years…" lists based on specific criteria.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To be eligible, a film must be an American motion picture with significant creative and/or production elements from the United States.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The film must be feature-length, defined as a minimum of 60 minutes in running time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The film must have had a theatrical release in Los Angeles County between January 1 and December 31 of the qualifying year.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The film must be in the English language or have English subtitles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The film must be publicly exhibited in a commercial theater for paid admission for at least seven consecutive days.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Once a film meets these criteria, it can be considered for inclusion on one of the AFI's various "best of" lists.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The films are chosen by a jury of experts in the film industry, including critics, academics, and filmmakers.  
[USER] User asked why the AFI only considers American films for their lists and mentioned that other countries also produce amazing movies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The AFI's main goal is to promote American filmmaking and celebrate the rich cultural heritage of American cinema, which is why they focus only on American films.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The AFI recognizes the contributions of international cinema and has created lists such as "AFI's 100 Years...100 Passions: America's Greatest Love Stories," which includes films from around the world.  
[USER] User expressed understanding of the AFI's focus on American cinema but thought it would be interesting to compare American movies to films from other countries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant acknowledged that it would be interesting to compare American movies to films from other countries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are many other organizations and publications that create "best of" lists that include films from all over the world, such as Sight & Sound's famous list of the greatest films of all time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The AFI's primary focus is on American cinema and cultural heritage, but there are many other resources available for those interested in exploring films from other countries.
